Update hydrological event state without weather forecast information

update_state_no_forecast.Rd

Computes the next state of a hydrograph event-detection finite state machine from the current state and the local flow dynamics, for the case where no weather forecast is available. The machine walks a storm event through the sequence BASEFLOW -> ONSET -> RISING_INFLECTION -> PEAK -> FALLING_INFLECTION -> RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW -> BASEFLOW, with an additional transition allowing a new ONSET during recession (re-onset).

Usage

update_state_no_forecast(prev_state, Q, dQ, ddQ, baseflow_Q, params)

Arguments

prev_state

Character scalar. The current state, one of "BASEFLOW", "ONSET", "RISING_INFLECTION", "PEAK", "FALLING_INFLECTION", "RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW".

Q

Numeric scalar. Current flow (e.g. m3/s).

dQ

Numeric scalar. First time derivative of flow (flow gradient). May be NA.

ddQ

Numeric scalar. Second time derivative of flow (flow acceleration). May be NA.

baseflow_Q

Numeric scalar. The current estimate of baseflow, used as the reference level for onset and return-to-baseflow thresholds.

params

A list of tuning parameters, evaluated within the function via with. Must contain:

onset_slope_thresh

Flow-gradient threshold for storm onset.

event_frac_thresh

Fractional rise above baseflow that also triggers onset.

eps

Tolerance on the gradient for detecting the peak (near-zero slope).

baseflow_tol_frac

Fractional tolerance around baseflow for declaring return to, and continuation of, baseflow.

Value

A character string containing the updated hydrological state.

A character scalar giving the next state. If no transition fires, prev_state is returned unchanged.

Details

Updates the current event state based on observed streamflow conditions and flow derivatives, using a finite-state machine adapted from the event detection framework of Wong and Kerkez. This implementation relies solely on observed discharge data and does not use weather forecast information.

State transitions are determined using flow magnitude (`Q`), first derivative (`dQ`), second derivative (`ddQ`), and an estimate of baseline flow (`baseflow_Q`). The possible states are:

  • "BASEFLOW"

  • "ONSET"

  • "RISING_INFLECTION"

  • "PEAK"

  • "FALLING_INFLECTION"

  • "RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW"

State transitions include:

  1. BASEFLOW \(\rightarrow\) ONSET

  2. ONSET \(\rightarrow\) RISING_INFLECTION

  3. RISING_INFLECTION \(\rightarrow\) PEAK

  4. PEAK \(\rightarrow\) FALLING_INFLECTION

  5. FALLING_INFLECTION \(\rightarrow\) RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW

  6. RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW \(\rightarrow\) BASEFLOW

Re-onset events are also permitted during the recession phase if flow rises sufficiently rapidly.

Transitions are driven by the flow magnitude and its first and second time derivatives:

  • BASEFLOW -> ONSET: triggered when the flow gradient exceeds onset_slope_thresh, or (as an extension not in Wong and Kerkez) when flow rises more than event_frac_thresh above baseflow.

  • ONSET -> RISING_INFLECTION: when the flow is accelerating (ddQ > 0).

  • RISING_INFLECTION -> PEAK: when the gradient flattens (abs(dQ) < eps).

  • PEAK -> FALLING_INFLECTION: when the flow is decelerating (ddQ < 0).

  • FALLING_INFLECTION -> RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW: when flow falls back to within baseflow_tol_frac of baseflow.

  • RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW -> BASEFLOW: when flow remains within baseflow_tol_frac of baseflow.

  • Re-onset: from either recession state (FALLING_INFLECTION or RETURN_TO_BASEFLOW), a renewed steep rise (dQ > reonset_thresh) returns the machine to ONSET. This is only described qualitatively in Wong and Kerkez.

If no transition condition is met, the current state is returned unchanged. NA values in dQ or ddQ suppress the transitions that depend on them.

References

Wong, B. P. and Kerkez, B. (2024). An adaptive storm-event sampling framework for high-frequency water quality monitoring.

Wong, B. P., & Kerkez, B. (referenced for the underlying state-machine formulation).

Examples

params <- list(
  onset_slope_thresh = 0.05,
  event_frac_thresh = 0.20,
  baseflow_tol_frac = 0.10,
  eps = 0.01
)

update_state_no_forecast(
  prev_state = "BASEFLOW",
  Q = 12,
  dQ = 0.08,
  ddQ = 0,
  baseflow_Q = 10,
  params = params
)
#> [1] "ONSET"

params <- list(
  onset_slope_thresh = 0.5,
  event_frac_thresh  = 0.2,
  eps                = 0.01,
  baseflow_tol_frac  = 0.1
)
update_state_no_forecast(
  prev_state = "BASEFLOW",
  Q = 10, dQ = 1.0, ddQ = 0.2,
  baseflow_Q = 5, params = params
)
#> [1] "ONSET"
